notes:
I couldn't write the notes. My first attempt fetched eight commentary pages at once, and that went over the tool's usage limit. When I tried again with just the Enduring Word page, I had no tool calls left. So I didn't read any pages on Hosea 9.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say, give a URL for every point and fill no gaps from my own knowledge. With nothing read, anything I wrote now would break those rules, so I've left out all verse notes.

**What I'd fetch next time, one page per call:**

1. **Traditional reading:**
   - enduringword.com/bible-commentary/hosea-9/
   - biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/hosea/9.htm
   - biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/hosea/9.htm
   - biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/hosea/9.htm
   - the Keil & Delitzsch page on biblehub
   - preceptaustin.org's Hosea commentary page
2. **Different traditions:**
   - Wesley's Explanatory Notes for Hosea 9 (studylight.org)
   - searches on gty.org, ligonier.org, desiringgod.org, thegospelcoalition.org, lcms.org and 1517.org
3. **Other views:**
   - netbible.org translator notes, which matter most for the hard verses: v. 1 (paid sex on threshing floors), v. 8 (the prophet as "watchman"), v. 10 (Baal-peor and "Shame"), v. 13 (the Tyre comparison) and v. 14 (the prophet's prayer)
   - bibleodyssey.org
   - newadvent.org, for the Church Fathers or the Catholic Encyclopedia on Hosea

If you ask again in a new message, I'll fetch these one at a time so I stay within the limit, then write the verse-by-verse notes with a URL for every point.
